messages:
sera: FYI onboarding run for GemmaX-8B-v2 hitting weird kvcache token-id shift when using the Qwen tokenizer mapping. outputs look garbled after 1024 tokens. attached logs below.
max: ugh. any repro script? can you paste the short log?
sera: repro command: `python bench_infer.py --model gemmax-v2 --tokenizer qwen_tokenizer --quant 8bit --seq 2048 --batch 1`
sera: log snippet:
```
[2026-03-18 15:02:10] kvcache: insert key. token_ids=[101, 2345, 78, 12, 0, 0]
[2026-03-18 15:02:10] decoder: rotary_phase_scaled=True base=1000.0
[2026-03-18 15:02:10] decode: output_ids=[101, 2345, 78, 12, 4096, 4096]  <-- unexpected high ids
```
ali: quick guess: tokenizer vocab mapping shifts IDs > 4096 into the reserved space? seen this with a half-baked merge script before. did you run vocab-convert with `--preserve-offsets`?
jordan: also check whether rotary-phase scaling is being applied relative to `rotary_dim` vs `head_dim`. Gemma variants use different rotary_base defaults than Qwen. mixing defaults will mess up positional interpolation and kv keys can become misaligned.
sera: i tested toggling rotary_phase scaling to `False` and the raw token ids then match, but perplexity jumps and we see quality regression on standard eval set (common-gen).
max: can you share eval numbers? little summary is fine.
sera: quick eval (subset):
- baseline (gemmax-v2 native tokenizer, rotary_phase True, 8bit): ppl=12.3, rouge-L=0.62
- cross-tokenizer (qwen tokenizer, rotary_phase True, 8bit): ppl=27.8, rouge-L=0.45 (garbled after 1k)
- cross-tokenizer (qwen tokenizer, rotary_phase False, 8bit): ppl=18.1, rouge-L=0.53
so disabling rotary_phase reduces the catastrophic failure but still worse than baseline.
max: suggests two issues: token id mapping (vocab offsets) + rotary phase mismatch. both can amplify when quantized. try canonicalizing token ids via `vocab-map --align-to model_vocab.json` before serving. also run 4-bit run to see if quantization amplifies offsets.
sera: ran 4-bit (nf4) quick: cross-tokenizer w/ rotary_phase True => immediate OOM on gemma runtime (weird). with rotary_phase False => runs but ppl=22.6.
ali: OOM might be runaway kv shapes if kv indexing is wrong; kvcache size grows because token ids map to huge embedding indices. that would cause weird mem growth and rotor misapply.
jordan: proposed small checklist:
1) regenerate vocab map with explicit offsets and verify max_id <= model_vocab_size-1
2) ensure tokenizer special tokens mapping matches model config (pad/unk/eos ids)
3) force rotary_base and rotary_phase params to gemma defaults when running cross-tokenizer experiments
4) run a short synthetic test: feed same string tokenized by both tokenizers and compare token ids and kvcache hash.
5) reproduce with a minimal CPU-only run to rule out quantization OOM interactions
sera: i'm on it. starting step 1+4 now, will post a tiny diff script.
eval-bot: auto-eval finished on subset: cross-tokenizer mapping check FAILED (token-id shift detected at pos 1024), delta_ppl=+15.3, flagged for triage.
sera: attaching small script I used: `scripts/compare_tokenmaps.py`
```python
# very small diff: compare_tokenmaps.py
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
A = Tokenizer.from_file('gemma_vocab.json')
B = Tokenizer.from_file('qwen_vocab.json')
text = 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog' * 40
a_ids = A.encode(text).ids
b_ids = B.encode(text).ids
# compare first mismatches and positions
for i,(x,y) in enumerate(zip(a_ids,b_ids)):
    if x!=y:
        print(i,x,y)
        break
```
max: perfect. run that and also run `python -c "import numpy as np; print(np.max(a_ids), np.max(b_ids))"` to see id ranges.
sera: quick run results: max_a=49999 max_b=65535 first_mismatch_pos=1024 mismatch pair=(120, 4096)
ali: bingo. qwen tokenizer seems to reserve a 4096-xxxx range for some byte-level tokens. mapping should clamp/translate those.
jordan: I'll open a small PR to the vocab-convert tool to add `--clamp-ids` and a warning if max_id>vocab_size. will also default rotary_base to gemma default when model name contains 'gemma'.
sera: thanks. will re-run full suite once PR lands. tagging @max for visibility. :thumbsup:
max: thanks, team. let's track in a follow-up incident thread if eval regressions persist. good triage. :+1:
